templates.name: Markdown ingestion and HTML rendering
templates.description: Given a test fixture directory with multiple .md files (including headings, lists, code blocks, links, and emphasized text), when the build command runs, then (a) build exits with code 0, (b) output directory contains one HTML file per input note (excluding configured ignores), and (c) rendered HTML preserves expected structure and formatting for each Markdown element as defined by the supported subset.

templates.name: Static site output constraints
templates.description: Given a successful build, verify the output contains only static assets (HTML/CSS/JS and static files), and no server-side runtime requirements are present. Validate that opening the site via a static file server (or file:// if supported) loads pages without runtime errors in a modern browser.

templates.name: Full-text search accuracy and responsiveness
templates.description: Given a dataset with known terms in titles and bodies, when searching for a term, then results include the correct notes with highlighted matches (if supported) and exclude notes without the term. Measure response time for search interactions and verify it remains within the target threshold at the confirmed scale.

templates.name: Tag extraction and tag browsing
templates.description: Given notes containing tags per the agreed convention, when the site is built, then (a) each note page displays its tags, (b) a tag index page is generated, and (c) each per-tag page lists all and only the notes containing that tag. Validate normalization rules (case/spacing) per spec.

templates.name: Internal links and backlinks generation
templates.description: Given notes with internal links per the agreed convention, when the site is built, then (a) internal links resolve to the correct destination pages, (b) each destination page includes a backlinks section listing all source notes, and (c) backlinks are clickable and navigate correctly. Verify handling of broken links per spec (warn/fail/render).

templates.name: Information architecture and navigation
templates.description: Given the required pages (home, all notes, tags index, per-note pages), verify all pages are generated and linked from navigation elements. Check that each page has correct titles, breadcrumbs (if required), and consistent layout per spec.

templates.name: Relative paths and hosting compatibility
templates.description: Given a configured base URL or relative path strategy, verify that internal links, asset references (CSS/JS/images), and search index loading work when hosted on the target static host (e.g., GitHub Pages).

templates.name: Build error handling and reporting
templates.description: Given malformed Markdown or invalid internal links per spec, when the build runs, then the tool reports clear, actionable errors or warnings, and build success/failure aligns with configured policy (fail on errors vs warn).

templates.name: CLI build workflow
templates.description: Given a standard invocation via the agreed interface (CLI, unless another interface is explicitly in scope) with input and output directories, verify help output, exit codes, and argument validation. Ensure builds can be run non-interactively, are documented and repeatable, and produce deterministic output.

templates.name: Browser Compatibility Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that the generated site loads and functions without errors in modern browsers (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) covering the expected user base.

templates.name: Markdown Flavor Support Acceptance
templates.description: Verify that the supported Markdown features (e.g., CommonMark/GFM, tables, code highlighting, etc.) render correctly in the generated site per the agreed scope.

coverage_guidance: Create a golden test fixture set that covers supported Markdown subset (headings, lists, code, links, images) and any extensions explicitly in scope.
Define and test the exact conventions for internal links and tags (including normalization rules); include edge cases such as spaces, casing, and nested paths.
Include at least one dataset sized to the confirmed target scale to validate search responsiveness and build time bounds.
Validate both correct backlink generation and broken-link behavior per the agreed policy.
Test output under the primary hosting target (e.g., GitHub Pages) with base URL configuration to catch path issues.
Verify accessibility/basic UX: page loads without console errors; navigation is consistent across pages.
If incremental builds/watch mode are later added, include regression coverage for changed-only rebuilds.
Test search functionality with representative edge cases (empty queries, special characters, very long queries, no results).
Verify tag parsing and normalization across all agreed conventions (e.g., YAML front matter, inline hashtags), including edge cases (empty tags, special characters, duplicates).
Test internal link resolution for all supported conventions, including cross-directory links and edge cases (self-links, circular links, links to non-existent notes).
Verify backlink generation includes notes with no backlinks and notes with many backlinks.
Test browser compatibility on the agreed set of browsers/versions, covering all interactive features (search, navigation, tag filtering).
Verify that the output is fully static (no server-side dependencies) by serving from a simple HTTP server or file system.
Verify that the site information architecture matches the agreed design (e.g., required pages and navigation) once Q4 is resolved.
Test handling of large note sets and edge cases (very large notes, many tags, deeply nested links) to confirm performance targets once Q3 is resolved.
Verify behavior for unsupported Markdown features per the agreed flavor/scope (warn/fail/fallback) once Q6 is resolved.
definition_of_done: All acceptance templates executed with passing results against the agreed conventions for links, tags, and Markdown subset.
Search accuracy and responsiveness meet the confirmed scale targets and thresholds.
Generated output is fully static and deployable to the target host without runtime dependencies.
Backlinks, tags, and navigation pages are present and correct for the fixture datasets.
Build errors/warnings align with specified policy and are clearly reported.
No critical browser console errors on modern browsers for the built site.
Build process completes successfully on the target environment(s) for a representative input corpus.
All blocking open questions (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q10) have been resolved and incorporated into the implementation and tests.
Performance, scale, and usability targets in the success metrics are met.
Documentation is delivered covering usage, supported conventions, and limitations.
merge_log: Selected the more specific ATT-* templates from draft set 1 as the canonical base and removed overlapping ATT-01..06 templates from draft set 2 to avoid duplication.
Added ATT-07 (browser compatibility) and ATT-08 (Markdown flavor support) from draft set 2 because these concerns were not explicit standalone templates in draft set 1.
Merged build-workflow/documentation intent from ATT-10 into ATT-CLI-UX-009 to keep a single workflow template without duplicating coverage.
